title: Hong Kong crypto exchange CoinEx shuts down after 9 years
dek: CoinEx, a Hong Kong-based crypto exchange operating for nine years, will cease operations in December. Founder and CEO Haipo Yang cited falling trading volumes, prolonged crypto downturn, rising compliance costs, and mounting security risks.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: CoinEx will cease operations in December after nine years, citing falling volumes, prolonged downturn, and rising compliance costs.
bottom_line: CoinEx's December closure deadline will require users to withdraw funds by that date. The exchange's decision to liquidate rather than seek acquisition or restructuring leaves open the question of whether independent regional platforms can survive without either substantial institutional backing or liquidity consolidation onto larger venues.
body: CoinEx, a Hong Kong-based crypto exchange, will cease operations in December after nine years in business. According to Cointelegraph, the platform cited falling trading volumes, liquidity constraints, prolonged crypto downturn, and rising compliance costs as reasons for the closure.
Founder and CEO Haipo Yang cited mounting security and compliance risks in the decision, per CoinDesk. Yang rejected a sale in favor of a clean ending, according to the outlet.

The closure reflects the operational pressures facing independent regional exchanges in a contracting market. Monthly compliance and security costs have outpaced trading revenue, and the extended bear market has eroded liquidity on smaller venues. CoinEx's exit follows a pattern of consolidation in crypto infrastructure as platforms struggle to sustain operations amid compressed trading volumes and heightened regulatory requirements.
